subject: standard errors in latent mediation models

messages.author: 438e7105452ccc11
messages.subject: standard errors in latent mediation models
parts:
hello yves and fellow lavaan users!
 
to begin with, i would like to thank everyone who is involved in the lavaan project. for poor graduate students like myself with not enough money to spend on software like Mplus or EQS having access to it has been a true blessing.
 
i am trying to teach myself a little more "advanced" SEM techniques (latent mediation/moderation, multilevel sem, finite mixture models, etc.) through easy simulations and was just wondering...  how does lavaan calculate the standard error of the indirect and total effects in a mediation with latent variables? is it through the delta method as well? i am using the following (very simple) code to simulate data and fit my model. if there are any mistakes i would appreciate the input :-)
 
model1 <-
 
     '#measurement model
    
     X =~ 0.5*y1 + 0.5*y2 + 0.5*y3
     M =~ 0.7*y4 + 0.7*y5 + 0.7*y6
     Y =~ 0.9*y7 + 0.9*y8 + 0.9*y9 
 
     #direct effect
     Y =~ 0.75*X
     
     #mediator
     M =~ 0.75*X
     Y =~ 0.75*M
    
     #variances
    
     X~~1*X
     M~~1*M
     Y~~1*Y'

datum <- simulateData(model1, model.type=sem, sample.nobs=5000)
 

fitz <-
 
     '#measurement model     
     X =~ NA*y1 + y2 + y3
     M =~ NA*y4 + y5 + y6
     Y =~ NA*y7 + y8 + y9 
    
     #direct effect
     Y =~ a*X
    
     #mediator
     M =~ b*X
     Y =~ c*M
    
     #indirect effect
      ab:= a*b
    
    #total effect
      total:= c + (a*b)
    
     #variances
     X~~1*X
     M~~1*M
      Y~~1*Y'
    

summary(sem(fitz, data=datum, mimic="Mplus"))

On Tuesday, March 19, 2013 10:09:55 AM UTC+1, o.olv...@yahoo.com wrote:
and was just wondering...  how does lavaan calculate the standard error of the indirect and total effects in a mediation with latent variables? is it through the delta
Yes, if se="standard" (the default), lavaan uses the delta method for all newly defined parameters (using the := operator). You could also use se="bootstrap".

fitz <-
 
     '#measurement model     
     X =~ NA*y1 + y2 + y3
     M =~ NA*y4 + y5 + y6
     Y =~ NA*y7 + y8 + y9 
    
     #direct effect
     Y =~ a*X
    
     #mediator
     M =~ b*X
     Y =~ c*M
    
     #indirect effect
      ab:= a*b
    
    #total effect
      total:= c + (a*b)
    
     #variances
     X~~1*X
     M~~1*M
      Y~~1*Y'
    

summary(sem(fitz, data=datum, mimic="Mplus"))

Note that you could also use the std.lv=TRUE option in the fitting function.

Yves.
